description.narrative: The Second Rijeka Gateway Project for Croatia development objective is to develop the capacity, financial performance, and quality of services in the port of Rijeka to meet growing traffic demand, through public-private partnerships, while facilitating urban renewal by enabling the relocation of port activities. There are three components to the project. The first component of the project is port terminal development. This component includes the extension of the existing Brajdica container terminal by about 330 meters; and construction of infrastructure for a 400 meter long Zagreb container terminal. The second component of the project is port service enhancement. This component includes support in concessioning selected terminals, equipment and technical services for information flow integration and secured port access, enhanced environmental response, and technical studies to prepare for the Masterplan implementation. The third and final component of the project is project implementation. This component includes the supervision of civil works activities, audit services for the project and support in procurement and project management.

The overall project development objective is to develop the capacity, financial performance, and quality of services in the port of Rijeka to meet growing traffic demand, through public-private partnerships.

title.narrative: Signed concession agreements for at least two port terminals (2011)

comment.narrative: <p>The BCT is being operated by the Adriatic Gate Container Terminal (AGCT) under a concession contract signed in 2011 and the tender for the concession of the ZCT was launched on March 4, 2019, with ongoing support from MTBS (they have been providing support in the preparation for concession and they will assist the PRA in the tendering process as well). The signing of the concession contract for the ZCT is expected by end of 2019.</p>

comment.narrative: <p>This objective was achieved in June 2013, when the civil works were completed and the Brajdica Container Terminal (BCT) was handed over to the concessionaire Adriatic Gate Container Terminal (AGCT). Following purchase and installation of the necessary equipment, the Terminal started its normal operations in early July 2013.</p>

comment.narrative: <p>The construction of the Zagreb Container Terminal has been completed as of May 23, 2019.</p>
<p>This indicator has not been met by the project closing date, but it is highly likely to be met once the Zagreb Container Terminal becomes operational.</p>

<p>This target has not been met by the closing date. Although the container capacity has been substantially enhanced since the beginning of the project (from 150,000 TEUs to 400,000 TEUs), due to circumstances outside of the Port of Rijeka Authority (PRA) -isruptive weather conditions, financial difficulties faced by the joint venture’s lead partner- the construction of the Zagreb Container Terminal and its concession could not be completed within the project life time. As of May 23, 2019, the terminal construction has been completed and the pertaining concession contract is expected to be signed by end of 2019 (and thus the indicator related to the port container capacity will be met in the future).</p>

Development of port environmental protection plan (2010)

comment.narrative:
<p>The Environmental Management System (EMS) has been operational since November 2013. The EMS enables continuous reduction of the overall negative environmental impacts and improves the environmental performance on all locations under the management of theRA (including the locations of Rijeka, Sušak, Brajdica, Bakar, Raša – Bršica and Omišalj. An Agreement defining cooperation in the field of environmental protection was supported and signed by the Management Boards of the main concessionaires. The Agreement regulates mutual relations, responsibilities and communication regarding environmental protection and proceedings in regular and emergency situations between the PRA and users of the port area.</p>
<p> </p>

comment.narrative:
<p>The quality of the works supervision was satisfactory throughout the project implementation. The contract for construction supervision of the BCT was performed by the consulting firm Investinženjering d.o.o.,  while the supervision of the ZCT civil works has been performed by Investinženjering d.o.o. and Royal HaskoningDHV Nederland B.V. Joint Venture. As per the contracts provisions, the supervising engineers submitted progress report on a monthly basis for each of the two terminals and played a significantole in making sure that the civil works were of appropriate quality, that remedial measures were taken in due time to reduce overall delays in implementation and that disputes between the constructors and the beneficiary were solved in amiable manner.</p>
<p>Thus, the construction contract for the BCT was completed with minor delays and very close to the estimate at contract signing. The construction of the ZCT has been completed as of May 23, 2019.</p>
